predecessors.name: Western Wei
predecessors.text: the Western Wei realm in Guanzhong, Gansu and Sichuan that Yuwen Hu handed to Yuwen Jue in 557

successors.name: Sui dynasty
successors.text: the whole Northern Zhou realm, abdicated to Yang Jian on 4 March 581

ledger.x: 557: the Western Liang remains a Zhou puppet.
557: Yuwen Jue founds the Northern Zhou at Chang'an.
571: Emperor Wu gives the Western Liang 'three provinces'.
576: Emperor Wu attacks Northern Qi again, by Pingyang.
577: the Zhou annexes the Northern Qi.
580: the Zhou finish the Huainan campaign.
580: the Zhou hold the Yangtze line.
581: the Western Liang passes to the Sui with the Zhou's abdication; the infobox lists the Sui as the third protector.
581: Emperor Jing abdicates to Yang Jian.

wars.name: Zhou-Qi wars
wars.outcome: Zhou victory: attacks with the Tujue failed in winter 563 (Jinyang, Pingyang) and winter 564 (Luoyang) and in fall 575 (Luoyang, 20 days), then Pingyang fell in winter 576, Jinyang around the new year and Ye in spring 577.

wars.name: Chen-Zhou war over Huainan
wars.outcome: Zhou victory: Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche at Pengcheng in spring 578 and the Zhou took the strip back in the winter of 579-580.

wars.name: Zhou campaign against the Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Crown Prince Yun led a campaign against the Tuyuhun in spring 576; no change of border is recorded.

wars.name: Yuchi Jiong's rebellion
wars.outcome: Yuchi Jiong and other regional commanders rose against Yang Jian in 580 and were put down; no territory changed hands.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier; the Chen frontier on the Yangtze-Huai strip moved by campaign in 573, 577-578 and 579-580; the Turkic, Tuyuhun and Qi-remnant frontiers are approximate.
